description: Large square patio umbrella on a single centre pole with a valanced canvas canopy and a weighted base plate -- the one module in the outdoor roof set carried on one pole rather than four corner posts.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Large square patio umbrella on a single centre pole, canvas canopy stretched over eight radial ribs down to a short valanced edge, heavy round weighted base plate Materials: Cream canvas canopy with faint dirt streaking along the rib lines and mildew spotting at the seams, a sun-faded panel on one side, powder-coated aluminium pole chipped to bare metal at the base.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: 526 triangles / 2 draw calls / 2 materials / 2 unique geometries against 4000 / 4 / 3 / 6. Forty-eight perimeter samples give a smooth scalloped eave at an eighth of the triangle ceiling.

featureReviews.notes: A square 4 x 4 m plan at the eave, not octagonal or round. Built envelope 4.000 x 2.800 x 4.000 m exactly. The square is a requirement rather than a style choice: the asset notes need edges that meet cleanly when several are placed side by side.

One tube mast on the canopy axis and no corner posts, which is what separates this module from the four-post bays in the same set. The pole lands mid-bay, so placed in a row these canopies meet at their edges and leave the corners open.

Valance bottom at 2.10 m and crown at 2.80 m, taken from the asset notes directly rather than measured off the plate. The derived collider confirms it end to end: its canopy slab starts at y 2.09, so a player walks under the rim and stops there.

A round weighted base r 0.28 sits flat on the ground and SURVIVES into the derived compound as its own cylinder part, which is the point - the asset notes call it a trip hazard a player should collide with, and a base that existed only in the render would not deliver that.

The canvas sags between eight radial ribs AND the eave scallops between the rib tips. The scallop was added after the first render: with a straight square eave the shallow canopy read as a flat slab with a skirt round it, which is a fair description of what a 0.55 m rise over a 2 m half-span looks like without it. The rise itself is fixed by the asset notes (2.10 edge, 2.80 peak) and was not changed to flatter the picture.

name: Square Patio Umbrella
nameTh: ร่มสนามสี่เหลี่ยม
notes: Part of a modular outdoor roof kit and sized to its grid: a 4 x 4 m canopy on the same 4 m module as the four-post bays, which divides the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles exactly 2 x 2. 4 m is a large commercial cafe umbrella rather than a domestic one, and it is deliberate -- the size is what lets this style be placed in a grid with the rest of the set instead of being a one-off. It is the one module in the set carried on a SINGLE CENTRE POLE, so it tiles differently from the four-post bays: placed side by side the canopies meet at their edges and leave the corners open, which is exactly how a real patio full of umbrellas covers ground, and it means the pole lands mid-bay rather than on the grid line. Canopy edge at about 2.1 m and peak at 2.8 m, so a player walks under the rim. Square rather than octagonal so that edges meet cleanly when several are placed together. The weighted base plate is part of the prop and sits on the ground: it is a trip hazard a player should collide with, not a detail to leave off.
